app.name: SteadyHum
app.tagline: Your appliances have a normal. SteadyHum learns it and tells you when it changes.

enroll.intro: Record the machine three times while it is working well, ideally at different moments of its cycle. Hold the phone in the same spot each time.
enroll.notLearned: A few more sessions are needed for a reliable normal.

enroll.addMore: You can add more sessions any time: the more there are, the tighter the warning.
enroll.tooLoud: Something nearby is far too loud, wait a moment.
enroll.clipping: The sound is clipping the microphone. Move the phone back a little.
enroll.learnFailed: I could not learn a normal from these recordings. Try adding another session with the machine running.

spectralFlatness.lower: The sound is purer and more tonal than usual.

spectralCentroidHz.lower: The sound is duller than usual.

spectralFlux.higher: The sound is less steady: it changes more than usual.
spectralFlux.lower: The sound is steadier than usual.

onsetPeriodicity.higher: The knocks are more regular than usual.
onsetPeriodicity.lower: The knocks are less regular than usual.

amplitudeModulationHz.higher: The hum pulses faster than usual.
amplitudeModulationHz.lower: The hum pulses slower than usual.

amplitudeModulationDepth.higher: The hum pulses more strongly than usual.
amplitudeModulationDepth.lower: The hum pulses less than usual.

peakFrequencyHz.higher: The dominant tone is higher pitched than usual.
peakFrequencyHz.lower: The dominant tone is lower pitched than usual.

peakProminenceDb.higher: A whine or squeal stands out more than usual.
peakProminenceDb.lower: The usual whine stands out less.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.headline: Audio never leaves this phone.
privacy.body: SteadyHum analyses sound inside the browser. There are no accounts, no server and nothing is uploaded. The only downloads are the app itself and the models.
privacy.storedTitle: What is stored on this phone
privacy.storedAudio: Audio clips: only if you turn them on, and you can delete them any time.
privacy.storedProfiles: The learned normal of each machine: numbers, not sound.
privacy.storedHistory: The history of checks and your answers.
privacy.disclaimer: SteadyHum is consumer information, not professional advice. It does not diagnose faults. Gas appliances must always be checked by a certified technician. It is not a medical or safety device.

what.title: Your appliances have a normal.
what.body: SteadyHum learns it by listening to your machine while it is fine, then tells you whether it still sounds the same.
what.honest: It will not tell you what is broken. That would not be honest: nobody can know that from a phone microphone. What it does know is when something has changed, and how to describe it in words you can act on.

privacy.title: Audio never leaves this phone.
privacy.body: All the analysis happens right here, in the browser. There are no accounts, no server and nothing is uploaded.
privacy.detail: What is stored is numbers, not sound: the learned normal of each machine and the history of checks. Audio clips are only kept if you turn them on.

effort.title: It asks for a few minutes up front.
effort.body: Learning a machine’s normal takes 3 recordings while it is running, about 3 minutes in total. Without that there is nothing to compare against.
effort.detail: After that, each check is 30 seconds.
effort.wifi: Opening the learning screen downloads about 23 MB of models, before you record anything. Better on wifi; after that it works offline.
effort.tip: To start, a fridge or a boiler works better than a washing machine: they sound steady. A washing machine has very different phases and they all need recording.

help.title: Help
help.intro: The questions that come up most, short answer first.
help.replayBody: The three panels from the first run: what it does, where the sound goes, and what it will ask of you.

whatBroke.q: Why will it not tell me what is broken?
whatBroke.a: Because it does not know, and saying so would be making it up. A phone microphone can tell you a machine no longer sounds the way it did; naming the failed part is a leap no model can make honestly.
whatBroke.b: What it does instead is describe how it differs — lower, more metallic, a new knocking — so you, or a technician, know where to look.

verdicts.a: "Normal": within what it learned. "Slightly different": a little outside its normal, possibly a phase you never recorded. "Different": clearly outside. "Unusable": too much noise to say anything at all.
verdicts.b: Neither "slightly different" nor "different" means broken. They mean changed from what you taught it.

confidence.q: What is the confidence on a result?
confidence.a: How much I trust that particular verdict — not the probability that something is broken. It drops when part of the recording was noisy, when the phone was not its usual distance away, or when I have not heard much of that machine yet.
confidence.b: It always takes the worst of those three, never their average: good learning does not make up for a half-discarded recording.

recording.a: Leave the phone in the same place every time, at the same distance. That is the single biggest factor: record up close one day and from the doorway the next, and the comparison stops meaning anything.
recording.b: With the machine running, nobody talking nearby, no music or TV in the background. And do not cover the microphone with your hand or the table.

unusable.q: It says it could not listen properly
unusable.a: More than 40% of the recording was noise that was not the machine: voices, music, a bang. Rather than hand you a result that does not hold up, it declines to give one.
unusable.b: Record again at a quieter moment.

falseAlarm.q: It says different, but the machine looks fine
falseAlarm.a: That happens, especially if the machine has phases you never recorded while teaching it: a motor starting, a drain pump, a defrost cycle.
falseAlarm.b: Tell it so with "actually fine" on the result screen. That adjusts the threshold for that machine. If you know it was a new phase, also add a learning session with the machine in that state.

levelGuard.q: It warns the phone is closer or further away
levelGuard.a: The overall level does not match what it learned, and that alone can trigger a false alarm. It does not invalidate the check, but it is worth repeating from the usual spot.

changed.q: I deliberately changed something about the machine
changed.a: New filter, moved it, had it repaired — its normal is now a different normal. Add learning sessions in the new state, or relearn from scratch from the appliance page.

offline.a: Yes, once the models are downloaded. That download is about 23 MB and happens the first time you open a screen that records, before you record anything; better done on wifi.
offline.b: After that it needs no internet: the whole analysis runs inside the browser.

data.a: On this phone, and nowhere else. No accounts, no server. What is stored are numbers — the learned normal and the history — not sound, unless you turn on audio clips yourself.

gas.q: Can I rely on it for something serious?
gas.a: No. SteadyHum is a hint, not a diagnosis, and it is not a safety device. Any gas appliance must be checked by a certified technician, smell or no smell, whatever this app says.

watch.title: Watch
watch.intro: Listens continuously and tells you if the sound drifts away from its normal. Leave the phone where you always do, plugged in.
watch.needsProfile: First teach SteadyHum how it sounds when it is working well.
watch.screenAwake: I will keep the screen on.
watch.screenMaySleep: This browser will not let me keep the screen on. If it sleeps, watching may stop.
watch.drift: The sound has been creeping up for a while. Not a spike: a drift.
watch.summaryNone: I heard nothing outside its normal.
watch.honest: An episode means it sounded different, not that something is broken.
watch.failed: I could not start watching. Check the microphone permission and try again.
